beliefs.practice: Use a single MongoClient (driver) instance per process and reuse it across requests (do not create a new client per HTTP request); set sensible timeouts such as serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000 and socketTimeoutMS=300000 when constructing the client.

Keep the cluster connection string/credential out of source control: read it from an environment variable (e.g. DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault at runtime; never write the real URI/value into files, logs or repo artifacts (.env.example should contain a placeholder).
Require TLS for all client connections (e.g. tls=true / tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in the URI or equivalent driver options) and verify server certificates to avoid MITM attacks.
Enable retryable writes (retryWrites=true) and implement idempotency keys for operations that must not be duplicated (or deduplicate on unique keys) to safely retry transient failures.

Choose an explicit readPreference and writeConcern appropriate to correctness/latency: use primary (or primaryPreferred) reads for freshest data and w=majority for durable writes where correctness matters; document and assert these in the client configuration.

Create a compound ascending index on { strategy_id: 1, timestamp: 1 } to support efficient time-range queries and aggregations per strategy; ensure the index exists before running aggregation-heavy workloads.

Add additional indexes for common filters: e.g. { strategy_id:1, event_type:1, timestamp:1 } or single-field indexes on event_type and strategy_id so match stages are covered and index intersection can be used.

If storing vectors for vector search, store them in a dedicated field as a flat float32 array (normalized if using cosine) and create a vector index with the cluster-supported algorithm (e.g. HNSW with parameters m and efConstruction) on that field; keep vectors immutable on write.

Model events as immutable documents with at minimum: type (signal/execution/outcome), strategy_id, ISO-8601 timestamp, pnl (signed numeric), and a deterministic id (UUID or composite of strategy_id+timestamp); include a monotonic trade_seq or insertion timestamp to guarantee ordering.
Prefer single-document updates/inserts to avoid multi-document transactions; when multi-document atomicity is required, use MongoDB transactions sparingly and monitor their performance impact.

Compute win rate, average P&L and total P&L using MongoDB aggregation pipelines (e.g. $match by strategy_id and date range, $group to compute counts/sums/avg); set allowDiskUse: true for aggregations that could exceed RAM.

For server-side cumulative or drawdown computations, prefer $setWindowFields (window functions) if available in the cluster version; if not, compute deterministic max-drawdown client-side from time-ordered cumulative P&L series.

When aggregating many documents, pipeline stage order matters: early $match and $project to reduce document size before $group or $sort; place $sort after $match and before windowing operations when possible to leverage indexes.

Use range-based (timestamp or trade_seq) pagination instead of skip/limit for large collections to avoid high-scanning costs; use the compound strategy_id+timestamp index to do efficient range scans per strategy.
Always call explain() on representative queries/aggregations in dev to verify index usage and adjust indexes or pipeline stage order if the query plan indicates collection scans or high memory use.

Implement client-side exponential backoff and jitter for retrying transient network errors (e.g. with an initial delay ~100–200ms, exponential factor 2, max attempts 3–5) and treat some server error codes as non-retryable.
Add a TTL index for ephemeral or debug events (createIndex({ created_at: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: N })) rather than deleting them manually when you want automatic expiration.

Enforce a collection-level schema validator (JSON Schema) to ensure required fields like strategy_id, event_type, timestamp and pnl are present and of the correct type to prevent corrupt/invalid events from being stored.

Monitor cluster resource usage and scale compute or I/O proactively: for a managed Azure DocumentDB cluster pick higher node size (e.g. M-series) or enable autoscaling to absorb ingestion spikes and avoid RU throttling.
Regularly back up or export critical trading data and the indexes (scheduled snapshots or periodic mongodump/mongoexport) and validate backups by doing test restores.

Sanitize and redact sensitive information before sending aggregated stats or event data to an LLM and include only the fields needed in the LLM prompt (avoid embedding raw connection strings, API keys, or PII in prompts).

Instrument and emit metrics for operation latency, error counts, index usage and document growth; integrate with Azure Monitor or your APM so you can detect slow aggregations and unindexed filters quickly.

Design the seeding and tests to be idempotent: test fixtures should insert documents with deterministic IDs or delete the created documents at teardown so repeated runs against the same database do not accumulate duplicates.

When combining vector similarity with predicate filters, perform the filter ($match) first (if selective) to reduce candidate set, then run vector search on the reduced set or use the DB’s integrated vector + filter search capability if available.
